story: Hakainde Hichilema ran for president five times and lost, once spending four months in jail on treason charges for failing to give way to the president's motorcade. In 2021 he finally won, inheriting a country that had just defaulted on its debt. He restructured it, and with copper prices high and the US and China competing for Zambia's minerals, the economy returned to growth. In 2026 voters gave him a second term, but not the way he hoped.

On 13 August Hichilema won about 61 percent, beating Brian Mundubile, a former provincial minister in his first run, who took 38 percent (Al Jazeera). The campaign was calm, but election night was not: police raided a location where Mundubile was present, exchanged gunfire and arrested 11 people including senior opposition figures, which the government linked to "militia activity." Attacks on election staff and ballot thefts led the commission to suspend vote counting nationwide, a first (Africanews). Mundubile alleged result forms were altered; EU observers called the vote largely peaceful but raised concerns. Analysts read Mundubile's strong showing as frustration that macroeconomic recovery has not reached household budgets, and as a warning about Hichilema's own drift toward heavy-handedness, a charge he made against his predecessor.
briefing.power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years with a two-term limit and needs over 50 percent to avoid a runoff; the National Assembly is elected at the same time.
briefing.holders: President Hakainde Hichilema (UPND), since 2021, re-elected August 2026.
